filename: 17 Things You Didn't Know Claude Design Could Do.md
title: Austin Marchese: seventeen Claude Design use cases
author: Austin Marchese
sections: Systems and iteration

The creator recommends extracting a reusable design system from an existing website and reusing it across technical and nontechnical outputs (0:00 to 1:22). Inline comments and drawings make feedback precise (9:10). He proposes divergent page or component variations followed by convergence on the preferred concept (10:19 to 11:15).
Seventeen uses

The examples cover systems, animation, 3D assets with usage mockups, old-document rebranding, event flyers, colour/type comparisons, HTML email templates, inline feedback, funnel mapping, multiple variants, clickable wireframes, cross-team comments, templates, client-branded proposals, lead magnets, resumes and final copy cleanup. The email example adapts variables to the authentication backend (8:21 to 8:57).
Limits and incentives

He distinguishes Design from general-purpose Code/Co-work/Chat, describes it as layout rather than native image generation (4:37), and recommends low-risk internal animations rather than an exact product launch video (1:32). This is an Anthropic-sponsored video with BuildPartner marketing. Productivity and tool-capability statements are the creator's claims, not independently tested facts.

filename: 25 Tricks to Level Up Claude Design in 13 Mins.md
title: RoboNuggets: twenty-five Claude Design tips
author: Jay, RoboNuggets
sections: Reference-led systems

The creator recommends extracting a system from owned assets or a reference, shortlisting three systems, naming suitable fonts, studying competitor copy and mixing selected design principles (0:35 to 3:57). He says a local Code skill can hold a system when web Design lacks direct local-file access.
Resources and polish

Intermediate tips cover external image/video generation, previous projects, annotated reference libraries, Impeccable, voice guidance, 21st.dev, React Bits, Canvas UI, coherent icon packs, editable SVG, Lordicon and Creators Toolbox (4:57 to 9:48). Counts, free-access descriptions and capabilities remain dated source claims; licences and accounts need separate verification.
Advanced workflows

Advanced tips cover selective Apple HIG guidance, GSAP, Code Design artboards, a slider-based tweak panel, word-timestamped transcript animations through Hyperframes, and a searchable reusable design asset index (10:15 to 12:39). The captured text does not include the full prompts shown on screen. The existing PDF resource map already records decisions on all 25 tips; this transcript adds preserved, searchable evidence rather than another installation mandate.

filename: How to Use Claude Design Better Than 99% of People.md
title: Jack: fifteen reference-led Claude Design hacks
author: Jack; surname/channel identity not established by capture
sections: Motion with a visible target

The creator recommends a reference clip plus brand assets and intent, then three style options for looping animation whose first and last frames match (1:17 to 3:30). Hover lifts, soft presses and counters are suggested as small quality details. Claims that these make every design premium are judgments, not measured usability results.
Brand and editable assets

He proposes one brand-guideline file informed by brandguidelines.net, deck.gallery, logosystem.co, Visual Journal and Rebrand Gallery. He describes Higgsfield generation and Linearity brand imports, editable layouts, templates and MCP integration (5:24 to 14:38). Account access, paid plans, legal reuse and current connector behavior were not verified in this ingestion.
Inspect the relevant part and flow

Fonts and icons come from Typewolf, Fonts In Use, WhatTheFont, Fontshare, Flaticon and Icons8; the transcript explicitly says to check licences (15:35 to 16:51). Section-specific galleries include Navbar Gallery, Footer Design, CTA Gallery, 404s Design, Unsection and Bento Grids. Mobbin and Refero are suggested for whole flows; 60fps.design for motion rather than static screenshots (17:35 to 20:54).
Critique, clarity and reuse

A Design Loop uses a critic against a concrete reference; a five-agent checklist is also mentioned, but its exact five roles are absent from the captured transcript (21:22 to 25:16). He advocates a glance test and lower text density, SlopMonster copy review, simplified technical language, original poster/3D experiments and searchable reusable design assets (25:48 to 34:28). His numerical ASD-STE100 descriptions are unverified. Agent consensus is not proof of quality and no unbounded loop is adopted.
actions: Reference clip plus brand for motion
